title: Speaker
summary: An organizer-focused profile: establish topics and audience fit, offer an enquiry route, then support it with practical details and recordings.

for: Experts who speak alongside their main work
notFor: Researchers whose talks are part of academic work (start from researcher)

cards.purpose: Introduce the speaker’s audience, useful outcome and signature subjects.
An organizer’s route to a speaking enquiry.
Formats, speaker kit and practical planning information.
Three or four recordings or appearances that demonstrate the work.
The press kit and selected professional channels.

slots.ask: What name do you want at the top of the page?
slots.write: Exactly as they give it. Never shorten or translate it.

slots.ask: In one line, what do you do and for whom?
slots.write: One sentence, at most 120 characters, no hashtags or emoji. This appears in the About popover, not beside the name; repeat the essential purpose in the first text card.

slots.ask: Who are your talks for, what should the audience take away, and what two to four subjects do you speak on? Give one line on your angle for each.
slots.write: Start with a heading and two sentences identifying the speaker, intended audience and useful outcome. Follow with two to four bold topic titles and a one-line angle. Use the speaker’s own scope and claims. Use only their confirmed information; replace or remove every demonstration name, claim, number, price, quote, date and URL in this field. Never keep sample copy as a fallback.

slots.ask: What should people know before taking this action: who it is for, format, timing, price or reply expectations, only if you want to publish them?
slots.write: One or two short sentences, at most 400 characters. Include only facts supplied for this action; do not assume an introductory call is free or that any date, price or reply time is current. Use only their confirmed information; replace or remove every demonstration name, claim, number, price, quote, date and URL in this field. Never keep sample copy as a fallback.

slots.ask: How should organisers book you: a booking page, an agent, email?
slots.write: First button = the booking page (hire preset). Agent addresses only with the agent's agreement. Only an address they confirm may be public: everyone can see it. Use only their confirmed information; replace or remove every demonstration name, claim, number, price, quote, date and URL in this field. Never keep sample copy as a fallback.

slots.ask: What short heading should introduce this action?
slots.write: Use a clear heading that describes the action; no unconfirmed availability or promise. Use only their confirmed information; replace or remove every demonstration name, claim, number, price, quote, date and URL in this field. Never keep sample copy as a fallback.

slots.ask: What formats do you offer, do you have a speaker kit, and how do you handle fees?
slots.write: Formats, kit link and fee policy as they state them. Never publish a fee figure unless they ask. Use only their confirmed information; replace or remove every demonstration name, claim, number, price, quote, date and URL in this field. Never keep sample copy as a fallback.

slots.ask: Which recent talks should be listed? Links to video are best.
slots.write: tag = event · year; title as delivered; description = format and whether video exists. Audience numbers only if the event published them. Select up to four featured entries for this page; link to the complete archive or catalogue instead of deleting the person’s remaining work. Use only their confirmed information; replace or remove every demonstration name, claim, number, price, quote, date and URL in this field. Never keep sample copy as a fallback.

slots.ask: Where else should organisers look you up?
slots.write: Account URLs only. Use only their confirmed information; replace or remove every demonstration name, claim, number, price, quote, date and URL in this field. Never keep sample copy as a fallback.

slots.ask: Do you want a place on your profile? A city or region is enough.
slots.write: As they write it. Never infer it.

slots.ask: Do you have a website of your own?
Do you have a photo, artwork or logo you want to upload as the profile picture?
slots.write: The person uploads their chosen picture in the editor. Never fetch, generate or infer a personal photo. Use their description for alt text wherever the editor asks for it.
